chunks: From him, from Al-Husayn ibn Yasar, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who acts as a guide/broker for houses and estates and takes a fee for it, he said: 'This is a fee, there is no harm with it.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهَا: There is no harm with it (it is permissible)
key_terms.وَالضِّيَاعِ: And estates/lands (specifically uncultivated or agricultural lands)
key_terms.يَدُلُّ: He guides or acts as a broker/intermediary

ai.seo_question: Is the commission fee for a real estate broker or house guide permissible in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validating the fee of a *dalal* (broker) for facilitating property transactions, establishing the principle of *ujrah* (compensation for service) in commercial dealings. This ruling underscores the permissibility of professional intermediaries in Islamic jurisprudence, provided the service is legitimate and the fee is agreed upon, reflecting the practical needs of the Muslim community's economic life. It serves as a foundational text for the legality of brokerage fees in Shia fiqh, distinguishing them from usury or unjust enrichment.
